title: Physical AI's Next Bottleneck Is Finding the Right Video — Rafael Levi, Bright Data
talk_summary: A Bright Data product talk about indexing web video by action so robotics/AV teams can search-first and collect only relevant clips, avoiding downloading and discarding huge volumes of video. The transferable core is the search-first/collect-second pattern and the measured waste rates from naive bulk collection.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of bulk-downloading a huge corpus and filtering after, they pre-index the corpus by the property you care about (actions) and return only matching snippets with timestamps and match scores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what we propose is search first collect second
takeaways.numbers: Nvidia discards ~96% of downloaded video; Stable Video Diffusion discards ~74%

takeaways.what_they_do: They quantify how much of the bulk-collected data is thrown away and frame that as wasted compute, bandwidth, storage and money; the fix is filtering before ingestion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: That's wasted compute. That's wasted bandwidth. That's wasted storage. That's just a lot of wasted money.

takeaways.technique: Return scored, trimmed snippets with provenance
takeaways.what_they_do: API returns the clip, timestamp, match score, frame count, and a link to the original source so consumers can verify and use directly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We provide to you this time stamp. We provide to you the score matching, how close it is to your query, and of course the frame count.

takeaways.technique: Query by semantics, not just keywords/titles
takeaways.what_they_do: They index by content/action rather than title keywords, so they find relevant material that keyword search on titles misses.
